question: Should `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` accept scheme-level wildcard entries such as `chrome-extension://*`, and what exact wildcard grammar is acceptable for the Gateway browser-origin authorization boundary?
rationale: This changes which browser origins may reach Gateway HTTP/WebSocket handling, and current docs intentionally describe full-origin allowlisting plus the global `*` as the only wildcard policy.

options.title: Approve constrained scheme wildcards
options.body: Define a small, explicit grammar such as vetted scheme-only extension patterns, implement it in the shared origin helper, and document allow/reject cases before accepting the feature.

options.title: Keep exact origins only
options.body: Reject scheme wildcards and rely on exact opaque-origin support plus the existing global `*` escape hatch for intentionally broad local testing.

options.title: Fold into origin-pattern design
options.body: Wait for the broader allowed-origin-pattern contract to settle, then decide whether Chrome extension scheme wildcards belong in that same config surface.

recommendation.title: Approve constrained scheme wildcards
recommendation.body: Define a small, explicit grammar such as vetted scheme-only extension patterns, implement it in the shared origin helper, and document allow/reject cases before accepting the feature.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced and repeatedly hardened the Gateway origin-check boundary, so he is the strongest routing candidate for this security/product choice.
